guide.summary: Use OAuth authorization code flow with the api_v3 scope on each customer's OpenProject instance, then read GET /api/v3/work_packages with offset/pageSize. api_v3 is the broad standard API grant, so only read calls should be made. Customer administrators must register the OAuth app on instances they manage. Provider review and distribution rules are not in the supplied sources and remain unknown.

findings.title: Authorization code flow for the connected person
findings.detail: The authorize endpoint takes client_id, redirect_uri and scope, then the code is exchanged at the token endpoint. Calls use a Bearer access token.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

findings.title: api_v3 is the broad standard API grant
findings.detail: api_v3 is the default when no scope is checked and is the standard API. No narrower work-package read scope is documented, so the token is broader than the read.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Customer administrators must register the OAuth app on their instances
findings.detail: The OAuth application is added in the instance's authentication settings, so an administrator of each customer instance must create it when the developer lacks that access.
findings.appliesWhen: The developer does not administer a customer's OpenProject instance.

steps.title: Implement the callback and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the redirect handler and the POST to the instance's /oauth/token endpoint using the authorization code grant. Keep the instance base URL as a user input.
steps.doneWhen: The exchange code can be sent to the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and redirect_uri.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--url 'https://example.com/oauth/token' \ --header 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:

steps.title: Authorize the representative test account and obtain a token
steps.detail: Open the authorize URL on the test instance and sign in as the representative test user. Approve consent, then exchange the returned code. Expected response: an access_token value.
steps.doneWhen: The test user's consent completes and the token response includes access_token.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

steps.doneWhen: The response is a work package collection and paging parameters are accepted, with only GET calls in the log.
